title: Common Question Words
lede: Ask for exactly the missing information—person, thing, action, place, time, manner, reason or quantity—and shape the answer to match.

blocks: ## A question word creates an information gap
Good communication depends on asking for the right category of information and recognising what the answer must supply.
[callout] Cambridge relevance: question words drive role plays and topic conversations and help readers identify what information a message, notice or dialogue requests.
Master the core words by meaning, then extend them with prepositions and natural follow-ups.
- Use مَنْ, مَا, مَاذَا, أَيْنَ and مَتَى.
- Match each question to an answer of the correct type.
- Use مِنْ أَيْنَ and إِلَى أَيْنَ for origin and destination.
- Ask follow-up questions and report answers.
- Recognise compact forms such as بِمَ and فِيمَ.
- Edit an interview for precision, flow and answer alignment.
Identify the information category required by each question.
Learn each word together with the answer shape it requires.

TABLE: Question word | Information requested | Model question | Answer shape // مَنْ | person | مَنْ هَذَا؟ | name, person or relationship // مَا | thing, identity, name/category | مَا اسْمُكَ؟ | noun or nominal information // مَاذَا | action or object | مَاذَا تَقْرَأُ؟ | verb phrase or object // أَيْنَ | place | أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ | place phrase // مَتَى | time | مَتَى تَبْدَأُ الْحِصَّةُ؟ | time/date expression // كَيْفَ | manner or state | كَيْفَ تَذْهَبُ؟ | method, description or state // لِمَاذَا | reason | لِمَاذَا تَتَعَلَّمُ؟ | لِأَنَّ... // كَمْ | quantity | كَمْ كِتَابًا قَرَأْتَ؟ | number or quantity phrase
[callout] Answer alignment: if the answer gives the wrong category, the communication fails even when every word is individually correct.
Both can mean “what”, but practical learner patterns make their main uses easier to control.

[callout] Accuracy note: Arabic permits some overlap between مَا and مَاذَا. The house pattern above gives learners a reliable functional distinction without claiming that every alternative is impossible.
## مَنْ: people in different sentence roles
مَنْ can ask who performs an action, receives it, owns something or accompanies someone.

TABLE: Role | Question | Answer // Identity | مَنْ هَذِهِ؟ | هَذِهِ مُعَلِّمَتِي. // Subject/doer | مَنْ فَتَحَ الْبَابَ؟ | فَتَحَهُ الْمُدِيرُ. // Object | مَنْ زُرْتَ؟ | زُرْتُ جَدِّي. // With whom | مَعَ مَنْ ذَهَبْتِ؟ | ذَهَبْتُ مَعَ أُخْتِي. // Whose/for whom | لِمَنْ هَذَا الْكِتَابُ؟ | هُوَ لِي.
## أَيْنَ, مِنْ أَيْنَ and إِلَى أَيْنَ
Prepositions distinguish static location, origin and destination.
[callout/warning] Do not answer all three with the same bare place name. Keep the preposition that expresses the relationship.
Ask when something happens, how someone feels or by what method an action occurs.
A why-question should lead to a reason, not simply another fact.
[callout] Extend further: reason + result creates cohesion: كُنْتُ مَرِيضًا، لِذَلِكَ بَقِيتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ.
Prepositions remain meaningful parts of the question and often shape the answer.

TABLE: Full form | Compact/formal form | Example // بِمَاذَا | بِمَ | بِمَاذَا / بِمَ تَكْتُبُ؟ // فِي مَاذَا | فِيمَ | فِيمَ تُفَكِّرُ؟ // لِمَاذَا | لِمَ | لِمَ تَأَخَّرْتَ؟ // مِنْ مَاذَا | مِمَّ | مِمَّ تَخَافُ؟ // عَنْ مَاذَا | عَمَّ | عَمَّ تَبْحَثُ؟
[callout] Core route: the full forms are clear and safe. Stretch: recognise the compact spellings in formal reading and use them when secure.
Repair mismatched question words, missing prepositions and answers of the wrong type.
Select the question word that makes the answer relevant.
Build an interview that moves from factual questions to explanation and follow-up.
Listen to a partner’s ten questions and tick the category you hear: person, thing, action, place, time, manner, reason or quantity.
مَا اسْمُكَ؟ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ مَتَى وَصَلْتَ؟ كَيْفَ سَافَرْتَ؟ لِمَاذَا زُرْتَ الْمَدِينَةَ؟
Match each question to a field on a visitor form.
Ask one question from each category. After every answer, ask a second question that develops the same topic.
Summarise your partner’s answers in the third person, checking pronouns and tense.
### Create and answer a topic interview
Write a twelve-question interview about daily life, family, school, leisure, travel and future plans, then provide model answers.
[callout] Success checklist: Use مَنْ, مَا, مَاذَا, أَيْنَ, مِنْ أَيْنَ, إِلَى أَيْنَ, مَتَى, كَيْفَ, لِمَاذَا and كَمْ; include past, present and future answers and at least four reasons.
Choose the question word and structure that match the missing information.
- Ask about people, things, actions, places, time, manner, reason and quantity.
- Distinguish مَا from the reliable action pattern مَاذَا + verb.
- Align answers with the information requested.
- Recognise useful compact preposition + مَا forms.
Spaced revisit: take a paragraph from a previous topic and write eight different questions whose answers are found in the text.
